FOREWORD
Because prayer is the raising of your heart and mind to
God, it is just as necessary for the life of your soul as
breathing is for the life of your body.
With the People of God you have to walk the same
road of Life. You praise, thank, and ask God for help.
At times you experience great joy in giving witness to
the life and teachings of Christ. Often, however,
spiritual, moral, and bodily miseries trouble your soul.
In such circumstances, St. Paul tells us, AWhen we
cannot choose words in order to pray properly, the
Spirit Himself asks for us; and God, who knows
everything in our hearts, knows perfectly well what
the Spirit desires.@ (Rom.8 . 26-27).
In this prayer book are found the expressions of a deep
faith in a just and merciful God, who heals broken
hearts, binds up mens wounds, frees the oppressed,
feeds the hungry, sets captives free, give sight to the
blind, supports orphans and widows, pardons all
faults, above allCand in spite our inconsistenciesC we
find a God who is faithful to his promises.
DAILY PSALMS AND CANTICLES is a book of hope, a
light to guide your way home. May your prayerful use
of it be for the greater glory of God and the salvation
of souls.
+ MICHAEL J. DEMPSEY, O.P.
Bishop of Sokoto
15th August 1972
HOW TO USE THIS BOOK
This book follows the arrangement of the Liturgy of the Hours, the official
prayer book of the Church. It contains a four week cycle of five daily prayers:
1) Morning, 2) Midday. 3) Evening, 4) Compline, and 5) Office of Readings,
which can be at any time. Of these the most important are Morning and
Evening Prayer.
Each hour begins with a call to prayer. For the first prayer of the day
(Morning or Office of Readings) it is Psalm 51:25, "Help me to speak, Lord.
And I will praise you." This is followed by the Invitatory Psalm (See p.9). For
the other hours, the call to prayer is Psalm70:1, "Save me God. Lord help
me now." This is followed by "Glory be to the Father... Amen. Halleluia."

Some Psalm Tones
SOME PSALM TONES
In this book the psalms are set out in strophes, or
paragraphs, each containing verses of 2 or 3 lines each. When the
Liturgy of the Hours is celebrated in common, two groups sing the
verses or strophes alternately. Some tones are meant for alternating
at each verse; others are for alternating after each strophe.
Strophic tones:
These tones are based on 4 lines fitting 2 verses. If the
strophe has only 1 verse the 1st and 4th lines are used, and the 2nd
if the verse has 3 lines. If the strophe has 3 verses, the last verse
repeats the 1st and 4th lines of the tone. When one of the verses
has 3 lines, the first line has a flex or is sung on a monotone followed
by a pause. The following are examples:

each line of your own section pause for two beats.
PSALMS AND CANTICLES
MOST FREQUENTLY USED
Invitatory
INVITATORY
Come, let us praʼise the Loʼrd!
Let us sing for joy to our proteʼctor and Saʼviour!
Let us come befoʼre him with thanksgiviʼng
and sing joyful soʼngs of praʼise!
For the Lord is a miʼghty Goʼd,
a mighty king over aʼll the goʼds.
He rules oʼver the whole eʼarth,
from the deepest caves to the hiʼghest hiʼlls.
He rules over the seʼa, which he maʼde;
the land also, which heʼ himself foʼrmed.
Come, let us bow doʼwn and woʼrship him;
let us kneel before the Loʼrd, our Maʼker!
He is our God;
we are the peʼople he looks aʼfter,
the flock for whiʼch he proviʼdes.
Listen today to what he says:
"Don't be stubborn, as your ancestors weʼre at Meriʼbah,
as they were that day in the deʼsert at Maʼssah,
There they put me to the teʼst and triʼed me,
although they had seʼen what I diʼd for them.
For forty years I was disgusted with those people;
I said, >How disloʼyal they aʼre!
They refuse to obeʼy my commaʼnds!=
I was angry and made a soʼlemn proʼmise,
>You will never enter the land where I would
giʼve you reʼst.=
Invitatory
SOME INVITATORY ANTIPHONS
Sun.1 & 3: Come, let us praise the Lord! Let us sing to God
who protects us. Halleluia!
Mon.1 & 3: Let us come before the Lord, giving thanks.
Tue.1 & 3: The Lord is a great king: come, let us adore him.
Wed.1 & 3: Let us adore the Lord, for it is he who made us.
Thu.1 & 3: Come, let us adore the Lord, for He is our God.
Fri.1 & 3: Give thanks to the Lord, for his great love is without
end.
Sat.1 & 3: The Lord’s is the earth and its fullness: come, let us
adore him.
Sun.2 & 4:We are the people of God,  the flock for which he
provides. Let us adore him, Halleluia!
Mon.2 & 4: Let us rejoice in the Lord; with songs let us praise
him.
Tue.2 & 4: A mighty God is the Lord: come, let us adore him.
Wed.2 & 4: Cry out with joy to God, all the earth: serve the
Lord with gladness.
Thu.2 & 4: Come before the Lord, singing for joy.
Fri.2 & 4: Indeed, how good is the Lord; bless his holy name.
Sat.2 & 4: Let us listen for the voice of the Lord and enter into
his peace.
Advent: Come, let us worship the Lord, the King who is to
come.
17-23 December: The Lord is at hand: come, let us adore him.
24 December: Know today that the Lord will come: in the
morning you will see his glory.
Christmas (Before Epiphany): Christ is born for us; come, let
us adore him.
Christmas (After Epiphany): Christ has appeared to us; come,
let us adore him.
Holy Family: Come, let us worship Christ, the Son of God, who
was obedient to  Mary and Joseph.
Mary Mother of God: Let us celebrate the motherhood of the
Virgin Mary; let us worship her Son, Christ the Lord.
Epiphany: Christ has appeared to us; come, let us adore him.
Baptism of the Lord: Come, let us worship Christ the beloved
Son in whom the Father was well pleased.
Invitatory
Lent: Come, let us worship Christ the Lord, who for our sake
endured temptation and suffering.
or: Today if you hear the voice of the Lord, harden not your
hearts.
Holy week: Come, let us worship Christ the Lord, who for our
sake endured temptation and suffering.
Good Friday: Come, let us worship Christ, the Son of God, who
redeemed us with his blood.
Holy Saturday: Come, let us worship Christ, who for our sake
suffered death and was buried.
Easter (to the Ascension):   The Lord is risen. Halleluia!
Ascension: Hallelulia! Come, let  us  worship Christ the Lord
as he ascends into heaven. Halleluia!
After Ascension: Come,  let  us  adore Christ the Lord who
promised to send the Holy Spirit on his people. Halleluia!
Pentecost: Halleluia! The Spirit of the Lord has filled the whole
world; come let us worship him. Halleluia!
Trinity:  Come,  let us worship the true God: One  in Trinity,
Trinity in One.
Body and Blood of Christ: Come, let us adore Christ the Lord,
the bread of life.
Sacred Heart: Come,  let us worship Jesus, whose heart was
wounded for love of us.
All Saints: Come, let us worship God whose  praises are sung
in the assembly of the saints.
All Souls: Come, let us worship the Lord; all things live for him.
Christ the King: Come, let us worship Jesus Christ, the King of
kings.
Te Deum
TE DEUM (Church’s Hymn of Praise)
Te Deum
Antiphons for Midday
Some Antiphons For Midday:
ADVENT
Before Noon: The prophets foretold that the Saviour would be
born of the Virgin Mary.
Midday: The angel Gabriel said to Mary, ‘Rejoice, most highly
favoured one! The Lord is with you. Of all women, you are the
most blessed’.
Afternoon: Mary was greatly troubled at this greeting and
wondered what it might mean. She said, ‘I am to give birth to a
King without ceasing to be a virgin’.
CHRISTMASTIDE Before Epiphany
Before Noon: Joseph and Mary, the mother of Jesus, wondered
at what was being said about him.
Midday: Mary treasured all these things and pondered them in
her heart.
Afternoon: My eyes have seen the salvation which you prepared
in the presence of all the peoples.
CHRISTMASTIDE After Epiphany
Before Noon: The mystery, which was hidden from earlier ages
and generations, is now made clear.
Midday: Christ came and preached peace to you who were far
off, and peace to you who were near.
Afternoon: I have appointed you to be a light to all peoples, to
be my saving power to the very ends of the earth.
LENT
Before Noon: This is the time of repentance for us to atone for
our sins and seek salvation.
Midday: As I live, says the Lord, I have no pleasure in the death
of the wicked man, rather let him turn from his evil way and live.
Afternoon: Armed with the justice which is the power of God, let
us prove ourselves with great patience.
EASTERTIDE
Antiphon: Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.
Hymns For Midday
HYMNS FOR MIDDAY
1. O Holy Spirit, ever one
with both the Father and the Son,
come now, O God, and spread, we pray,
your presence in our hearts today.
Let flesh and heart and lips and mind
sound forth our witness to mankind,
and love light up our mortal frame
till others catch the living flame.
Dear Father, grant us what we ask
through Jesus Christ, your Word of love,
whose Spirit makes us ever praise
one God, the king of all the world.
2. O mighty Ruler, faithful God,
you guide the day and all it brings
from dawn's bright splendour fresh with hope
to noontime's trying heat and sweat.
Put out the flames of angry strife,
remove the heat of wrong desire,
restore our bodies' health and strength
and guard our hearts in lasting peace.
Dear Father, grant us what we ask
through Jesus Christ, your Word of love,
whose Spirit makes us ever praise
one God, the king of all the world.
3. O God, creation's mighty force,
the master of all passing things,
you make all things result in good
for those who love and trust in you.
As day recedes, please give us light
to keep our life from fading out;
let love keep driving us in hope
till death brings glory without end.
Dear Father, grant us what we ask
through Jesus Christ, your Word of love,
whose Spirit makes us ever praise
one God, the king of all the world.

Solemn Feasts:

WEEKLY PRAYERS
WEEKLY PRAYERS
1. Father of love,
Hear our prayers.
Help us to know your will
And to do it with courage and faith.
2. Father of heaven and earth,
Hear our prayers,
And show us the way to peace in the world.
3. All-powerful and ever-living God,
Direct your love that is within us,
That our efforts in the name of your Son
May bring mankind to unity and peace.
4. Lord our God,
Help us to love you with all our hearts
And to love all men as you love them.
5. Father, watch over your family
And keep us safe in your care,
For all our hope is in you.
6. God our Father,
You have promised to remain for ever
With those who do what is just and right,
Help us to live in your presence.
7. Father,
Keep before us the wisdom and love
You have revealed in your Son,
Help us to be like Him
In word and deed, for he lives…
8. Lord, guide the course of world events
And give your Church the joy and peace
Of serving you in freedom.
9. Father, your love never fails,
Hear our call,
Keep us from danger
And provide for all our needs.
10. God of wisdom and love,
Source of all good,
Send your Spirit to teach us your truth
And guide our actions
In your way of peace.
WEEKLY PRAYERS
11. Almighty God, our hope and our strength,
without you we falter.
Help us to follow Christ
and live according to your will.
12. Father,
guide and protect your people,
grant us an unfailing respect for your name,
and keep us always in your love.
13. Father, you call your children
to walk in the light of Christ.
Free us from darkness
and keep us in the radiance of your truth.
14. Father, through the obedience of Jesus,
your servant and your Son,
you raised a fallen world.
Free us from sin
and bring us the joy that lasts forever.
15. God, our Father, your light of truth
guides us to the way of Christ.
May all who follow him
reject what is contrary to the gospel.
16. Lord, be merciful to your people,
Fill us with your gifts
and make us always eager to serve you
in faith, hope, and love.
17. God our Father and protector,
without you nothing is holy,
nothing has value.
Guide us to everlasting life
by helping us to use wisely
the blessings you have given to the world.
18. Father of everlasting goodness,
our origin and guide,
be close to us and hear the prayers of all who praise you.
Forgive our sins and restore us to life.
Keep us safe in your love.
19. Almighty and ever living God,
your spirit made us your children,
confident to call you Father.
Increase your Spirit within us
and bring us to our promised inheritance.
WEEKLY PRAYERS
20. God our Father,
may we love you in all things and above all things
and reach the joy you have prepared for us
beyond all our imagining.
21. Father, help us to seek the values
that will bring us lasting joy in this changing world.
in our desire for what you promise
make us one in mind and heart.
22. Almighty God,
every good thing comes from you
Fill our hearts with love for you
Increase our faith,
and by your constant care
protect the good you have given us.
23. God our Father, you redeem us,
and make us your children in Christ.
Look upon us,
give us true freedom
and bring us to the inheritance you
promised.
24. Almighty God our creator and guide,
may we serve you with all our hearts
and know your forgiveness in our lives.
25. Father, guide us, as you guide creation
according to your law and love.
May we love one another
and come to perfection in the eternal life prepared for us.
26. Father you show your almighty power
in your mercy and forgiveness.
Continue to fill us with your gifts of love.
Help us to hurry towards the eternal life you promise
and come to share in the joys of your kingdom.
27. Father, your love for us
surpasses all our hopes and desires.
Forgive our failings,
keep us in your peace and lead us in the way of salvation.
28. Lord, our help and guide,
make your love the foundation of our lives.
May our love for you express itself
in our eagerness to do good for others.
WEEKLY PRAYERS
29. Almighty and ever living God,
our source of power and inspiration,
give us strength and joy
in serving you as followers of Christ,
who lives and reigns...
30. Almighty and ever living God,
strengthen our faith, hope, and love.
May we do with loving hearts what you ask of us
and come to share the life you promise.
31. God of power and mercy, only with your help
can we offer you fitting service and praise.
May we live the faith we profess
and trust your promise of eternal life.
32. God of power and mercy,
protect us from all harm,
give us freedom of spirit
and health in mind and body
to do your work on earth.
33. Father of all that is good,
keep us faithful in serving you,
for to serve you is our lasting joy.
34. Lord, increase our eagerness to do your will
and help us to know the saving power of your love.
